Arete

I designed Arete as a connected care journey, from finding a provider to getting a prescription filled. I wanted to work through the handovers that can make a healthcare experience confusing.

01What I wanted to solve

I worked across patient access, consultations, HMO coverage and pharmacy fulfilment. The design also needed clear status language, recovery paths and consideration for localisation and poor connections.

02The decisions that mattered

Continue past the appointment.

I mapped the journey through coverage, prescriptions, pharmacy availability and continued care.

Explain coverage before commitment.

I made membership and plan limits visible while keeping Skip for Now available to uninsured patients.

Design the difficult states too.

I included verification errors, pending approvals, unavailable stock and recovery steps alongside the happy path.

03See the work

The screens below show how those decisions came together.

More screens and supporting work +

04What I can show, and what I would test

The case study’s evidence is the connected journey, state designs and component system. I would test coverage comprehension with patients, then validate insurer and pharmacy handovers. The interface alone cannot establish those services work.
